paragraphs.source_en: After admiring the first frost at Jurakudai in Uchino, Toyotomi Hideyoshi returned from Kyoto to Osaka at the end of the ninth month of Tenshō 14. Hideyoshi was exceptionally busy that year. A new age was dawning in history, and for him personally it marked the beginning of a glorious life; now was the moment for the Regent to embark upon his magnificent enterprise.

paragraphs.source_en: The nine-story keep of Osaka Castle had already astonished the world; the boundless wealth the Regent would display thereafter would amaze the whole realm still more, and the conviction that a new age had arrived had taken deep root in people's minds. From Kyoto and Osaka to the port of Sakai, everyone acknowledged Hideyoshi as the ruler of the realm. Yet one obstacle continued to trouble Hideyoshi on the road to realizing his grand ambition: where Tokugawa Ieyasu's allegiance would ultimately lie.
